title: Revolution or Hype? Seeking the Limits of Large Models in Hardware Design
problem: Recent breakthroughs in Large Language Models and Large Circuit Models have created excitement about AI's potential in EDA, but significant skepticism remains about practical capabilities versus inflated expectations.
motivation: The EDA community needs authoritative guidance on realistic capabilities and limitations of AI models in hardware design to make informed investment and adoption decisions.
method: The paper brings together experts from universities and companies to determine what large AI models can actually accomplish for circuit design and where they fail. It examines three core questions: reliability (can you trust the AI's results?), scalability (does it work for large, complex designs?), and interpretability (can engineers understand why the AI made each choice?). The overarching goal is to assess whether these AI models outperform the traditional computer-aided design tools we already use, or whether they work better when combined with existing methods.
key_novelty: This is an authoritative overview assessing what large language models and AI circuit models can and cannot actually achieve in chip design.
contributions: Critical analysis of practical capabilities and limitations of large AI models in EDA
Examination of reliability concerns in AI-assisted hardware design
Discussion of scalability and interpretability challenges
Perspective on complementarity vs. replacement of traditional EDA methods
limitations: Panel/overview paper without novel technical contributions; serves primarily to synthesize existing opinions; lacks empirical validation of claims.
primary_theme: AI models in hardware design: capabilities and limitations
